source_text: Στίχ. λς΄. Καὶ οἱ ἄνθρωποι. Οἱ τὴν γῆν ψέγοντες, ψεύστην τὸν Θεὸν, κατʼ αὐτοὺς εὐσεβῶς, ἔδειξαν, ἐπαινοῦντα (22) τὴν Παλαιστίνην.
thought_title: The spies made God a liar by slandering the land
orientation: Origen is commenting on Numbers 13:32, where the spies who scouted the promised land brought back a bad report, and he draws the moral conclusion that they made God a liar.
pass_a_gloss: Verse 36. And the men. Those who slander the land, according to them piously, showed God a liar, who praises the promised land.

choices.why: The glossary specifies 'made God a liar' as the rendering for this expression; the word order in Greek places the predicate adjective first for emphasis, but English requires the article before God.

The phrase is ironic: Origen says that in their own view they acted piously, but in reality they made God a liar. The adverb εὐσεβῶς modifies the showing, and κατʼ αὐτοὺς limits the claim to their own perspective.
The verb δείκνυμι means 'to show' or 'to make manifest'; here it means they demonstrated or made God out to be a liar by their slander.
The participle is present active, describing God as the one who praises the land; the present tense suggests ongoing or characteristic praise.
The glossary specifies 'the promised land' as the rendering for Παλαιστίνην, banning 'Palestine' and 'the land of Canaan'.

bible_refs.note: The verse reference Στίχ. λς΄ (verse 36) points to the Septuagint numbering of Numbers 13, where the spies bring a bad report of the land; the slander of the land is the subject of Numbers 13:32 in modern numbering.

pass_b_english: Verse 36. And the men. Those who slandered the land, piously in their own view, showed God—who praised the promised land—to be a liar.

problems.quote: God, who praises the promised land
problems.why: Greek says the men praised the promised land, not God; English reverses agency.
problems.fix: Those who slandered the land, piously in their own view, showed God to be a liar while they praised the promised land.
problems.ruling: ἔδειξαν...ψεύστην τὸν Θεὸν...ἐπαινοῦντα: men showed God a liar, praising Palestine; English wrongly makes God the praiser.

problems.why: God praised the land, not the spies. ἐπαινοῦντα is accusative, agreeing with Θεόν, not the slanderers.
